relationship.statement: A simple pendulum's swing period increases with the square root of its length and decreases with gravity, while bob mass has no effect.
assumptions: Both pendulums start from a small 20 degree angle.
Air resistance, pivot friction, and rod mass are neglected.
The reference pendulum stays fixed at 1.0 m on Earth.

quantities.label: Rod length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot to the test pendulum bob

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration pulling the bob downward

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the test pendulum bob

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from vertical for both pendulums, fixed at 20 deg

quantities.label: Reference length
quantities.meaning: Rod length of the fixed reference pendulum, 1.0 m

quantities.label: Test period
quantities.meaning: Time for one full back-and-forth swing of the test pendulum

quantities.label: Reference period
quantities.meaning: Fixed period of the 1.0 m Earth reference pendulum

quantities.label: Test angle
quantities.meaning: Current angle of the test pendulum from vertical

quantities.label: Test speed
quantities.meaning: Current speed of the test pendulum bob

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum speed of the test bob at the bottom of its swing

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = inputs.length; var g = inputs.gravity; var m = inputs.mass; var theta0 = 20 * Math.PI / 180; var omega = Math.sqrt(g / L); var period = 2 * Math.PI / omega; var theta = theta0 * Math.cos(omega * t); var dtheta = -theta0 * omega * Math.sin(omega * t); var bobX = 1.0 + L * Math.sin(theta); var bobY = -L * Math.cos(theta); var speed = Math.abs(L * dtheta); var maxSpeed = L * theta0 * omega; var vScale = 0.35; var vx = L * dtheta * Math.cos(theta); var vy = L * dtheta * Math.sin(theta); var velTipX = bobX + vScale * vx; var velTipY = bobY + vScale * vy; var angleDeg = theta * 180 / Math.PI; var bobSize = 0.2 + 0.8 * ((m - 0.5) / 4.5); var refL = 1.0; var refG = 9.8; var refOmega = Math.sqrt(refG / refL); var refPeriod = 2 * Math.PI / refOmega; var refTheta = theta0 * Math.cos(refOmega * t); var refX = -1.0 + refL * Math.sin(refTheta); var refY = -refL * Math.cos(refTheta); var refAngleDeg = refTheta * 180 / Math.PI; var isSlower = period > refPeriod + 0.05; var isFaster = period < refPeriod - 0.05; return { bobX: bobX, bobY: bobY, velTipX: velTipX, velTipY: velTipY, bobSize: bobSize, period: period, angleDeg: angleDeg, speed: speed, maxSpeed: maxSpeed, refX: refX, refY: refY, refPeriod: refPeriod, refAngleDeg: refAngleDeg, isSlower: isSlower, isFaster: isFaster }; }

always: Longer rod slows the swing down.
Bob mass does not change period.

lesson.title: What changes how a pendulum swings?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum against a fixed Earth reference as you vary rod length, gravity, and bob mass. Watch both the side-by-side swing and the angle plot.
lesson.instructions: Adjust rod length, gravity, and bob mass with the sliders. Compare the test pendulum's motion and wave against the fixed 1.0 m Earth reference, and pause or scrub time to inspect any moment.
lesson.goal: Learn that pendulum period depends only on rod length and gravity, not on the mass of the bob.
